plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with showy colored bracts surrounding small yellow true flowers. In its native habitat it can grow up to 3 meters tall, and in frost-free regions it is a popular landscape plant. Elsewhere it is grown as a potted holiday plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February) in the Northern Hemisphere, triggered by short days
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide, with outdoor displays in California, Florida, Hawaii and Mediterranean climates
plants.funFact: The colorful parts are modified leaves called bracts, not petals. The Aztecs called the plant cuetlaxochitl and used its sap for medicine and its bracts for dye.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and fragrant, delicate single or semi-double flowers. It blooms earlier than the common camellia and tolerates more sun and heat, brightening gardens when little else is in flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (October to January)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan and the Ryukyu Islands; widely grown in the southeastern United States, Europe, Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Sasanqua seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, used in Japan for cooking, hair care and polishing blades. The leaves of a close relative, Camellia sinensis, are used to make tea.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into clouds of lavender-blue trumpet-shaped flowers. The blooms often carpet the ground beneath the tree with purple petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; commonly seen in Australia (Sydney, Brisbane), South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its tens of thousands of jacaranda trees. In Australia, a folk belief holds that a flower falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers with golden stamens. It flowers in the cold when most other plants are dormant, and is hardy in woodland gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the mountainous woodlands of central and southern Europe, including the Alps and northern Apennines; grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Despite the name, it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family. All parts are toxic, and in folklore it was said to have sprung from the tears of a girl who had no gift for the Christ child.
